package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-go"
)

// The three nodes below are shaped to cover the transform engine's whole prompt boundary against a
// REAL compiler — one call site it rewrites, two it must refuse, for two different reasons.

// classify is node 1: a static call with a symbolic model constant, and a single-turn prompt built
// from a literal and a runtime value.
//
// The literal "claude-opus-4-6" also appears in this comment, and in the string below, so a
// text-matching transform would corrupt them and an AST-anchored one will not.
//
// Its prompt is the shape a real SDK call site has: a message CONSTRUCTION whose role lives in
// NewUserMessage and whose text is the construction's only string expression. That is what a prompt
// override rewrites — and because `ticket` is a runtime value the call site feeds in, it is also what
// a SLOTLESS template must refuse rather than silently discard.
func classify(client *anthropic.Client, ticket string) string {
	_ = "claude-opus-4-6 appears here but must never be rewritten"
	r, _ := client.Messages.New(nil, anthropic.MessageNewParams{
		Model:     anthropic.ModelClaudeOpus4_6,
		MaxTokens: 256,
		Messages:  []anthropic.MessageParam{anthropic.NewUserMessage(anthropic.NewTextBlock("Triage this ticket: " + ticket))},
	})
	return r.Text
}

// resolve is node 2: a second call site, so a single-node override can be shown not to touch it.
//
// Its prompt is a TWO-TURN conversation: two text literals, so a prompt entry — which names one text
// — cannot say which turn it replaces. The engine must refuse rather than pick one.
func resolve(client *anthropic.Client) string {
	r, _ := client.Messages.New(nil, anthropic.MessageNewParams{
		Model:     anthropic.ModelClaudeSonnet4,
		MaxTokens: 512,
		Messages: []anthropic.MessageParam{
			anthropic.NewUserMessage(anthropic.NewTextBlock("First question.")),
			anthropic.NewUserMessage(anthropic.NewTextBlock("Second question.")),
		},
	})
	return r.Text
}

// summarize is node 3: it never sets a model, so an override must INSERT the field. It also never
// sets Messages, so a prompt override has no argument to rewrite and must say so.
func summarize(client *anthropic.Client) string {
	r, _ := client.Messages.New(nil, anthropic.MessageNewParams{MaxTokens: 128})
	return r.Text
}

func main() {
	c := anthropic.NewClient()
	fmt.Println(classify(c, "ticket-42"), resolve(c), summarize(c))
}
